title.narrative: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Line of Credit Project

description.narrative: The proposed project is a line of credit through 13 participating financial institutions (PFIs) to targeted small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sri Lanka, including SMEs that are led by women, are first-time borrowers, do not sufficient collateral and are located outside of Colombo. The fund allocation for 10 PFIs has been made on a competitive basis. The project also includes an attached technical assistance (TA) for (i) developing innovative financial schemes for SMEs and promoting export-oriented cluster development (funded by the Japan Fund for Poverty Reduction (JFPR) and (ii) developing an ecosystem for women entrepreneurship in Sri Lanka (funded by the Women Entrepreneurs Finance Initiative (We-Fi).

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2017, at least one cluster-based loan presented to the banks (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.2.2, OP 6.1.2) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Completed. One cluster-based loan to fruits and vegetable cluster was presented to a bank in 2017 and another cluster-based loan to tea cluster was presented to a bank in 2020. Data Source: Consultant's final report

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2020, at least 450 women entrepreneurs registered for online learning and development platform to support networking and mentoring for women entrepreneurs (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1, OP 1.2.1, OP 2.2.1, OP 2.3.1) Achievement: 475 Progress/Status: Completed. Online platform “SME connect” (https://smeconnect.lk/#/ ) for learning, mentoring and networking was launched on 20 October 2022. As the first stage, the platform was used to conduct the online trainings for women SMEs from April 2021. 16 partner institutions were on board and signed MOUs. 907 women entrepreneurs were registered in the platform as of 30 September 2024. Data Source: Consultant's final report

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2020, at least 750 actual and potential female entrepreneurs from SMEs trained in business development and management (including financial literacy) (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1, OP 1.1.1, OP 1.2.1, OP 2.3.1) Achievement: 220 Progress/Status: Completed. 1,027 female entrepreneurs from various sectors were trained in business development and management (out of which, 557 were trained under the JFPR and 470 were trained under the We-Fi) as of 30 June 2022. Data Source: Consultant's final report

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2022, at least 1,000 subborrowers of working capital credit line submitted financial records through PFIs to PMU (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 6.1.4) Progress/Status: Completed. Recieved 1,395 financial records as of 30 June 2024. Data Source: Consultant's final report Actual value:

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2023, at least one new loan scheme to strengthen value chain linkage between tea factories and tea smallholders developed (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.2.2) Progress/Status: Completed. Two new tea value chain based financial products were proposed developed and discussed with the 13 PFIs while 6 PFIs provided positive feedbacks. Considering the final discussions, pilot product is proposed to launch with 3 PFIs using the reflow funds of the tea component. Data Source: Consultant's final report Actual value:

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2024, at least 1,500 growers from tea smallholding segment, including 500 women, accessed through mobile application platform (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1, OP 1.1.1, OP 1.2.1, OP 2.2.1, OP 2.3.1, OP 5.2.3, OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: On track. The TA is preparing a design for the mobile application platform. Consultants finalized the report on mobile application design as of 31 December 2023. IT firm (Firm 3) has completed the application development and released for User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Data Source: Consultant's final report Actual value:

Output: Capacity of SMEs in targeted clusters to access financial services enhanced Indicator: By 2024, at least 1,500 growers from tea smallholding segment, including 500 women, trained in financial literacy trainings (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1, OP 1.1.1, OP 1.2.1, OP 2.2.1, OP 2.3.1, OP 6.2.4) Progress/Status: Completed. Pilot training programmes commenced in March 2022. 102 tea smallholders, including 22 women trained in financial record keeping. Roll-out of the training conducted during February - September 2023 with 1,505 tea smallholders, including 490 women trained.Overall, 1,607 tea smallholders completed the training programs including 512 women participants. Data Source: Consultant's final report Actual value:

Output: Evidence based on women entrepreneurship development to inform future policymaking strengthened Indicator: By 2023, four national and regional seminars in total held to disseminate findings on women entrepreneurship development challenges and solutions (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.1) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Completed. 1) A national seminar on access to finance was conducted in partnership with Women's Chamber of Industry and Commerce Sri Lanka (WCIC) on 10 September 2019 with 100 women entrepreneur participation. 2) During Q2 2024, awareness workshop was conducted2 for We-Fi Code with the participation of PFIs, key stakeholders of we-fi code and development partner institutions. The progress of the We-Fi was presented. 3) In February 2025, a seminar was held in the Matara district to raise awareness about the SME Connect platform, targeting women entrepreneurs. The event was organized with the support of the National Enterprise Development Authority (NEDA) and the Matara District Secretariat. Nearly 200 women entrepreneurs participated, along with NEDA development officers from the Southern Province. 4) During May 2025, awareness on the SME Connect Platform and access to credit guarantees for women entrepreneurs has been conducted in Gampaha district. The event was organized by NEDA and staff from National Credit Guarantee Institution Limited also joined as resource personnel. 76 women entrepreneurs participated for the workshop. Data Source: Consultant's final report

Output: Evidence based on women entrepreneurship development to inform future policymaking strengthened Indicator: By 2023, one impact evaluation report submitted to the SME steering committee (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.2, OP 6.1.2) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed. Impact evaluation on the effectiveness of business development trainings was carried out and the final report was shared with the government. Data Source: Steering committee minutes

Output: Gender-inclusive policy and regulatory framework and support enhanced Indicator: By 2020, at least 25% of government staff surveyed in the three agencies completing action plans to support women entrepreneurship report higher levels of awareness of gender-specific challenges in women's entrepreneurship (2015 baseline: not available) (OP 2.3.2, OP 6.1.1) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed. Training materials and surveys were developed. Trainings were conducted for 216 staff of 3 government agencies. 63.4% of the persons surveyed developed action plans to support women entrepreneurs and reported higher level of awareness of gender specific challenges.
Data Source: Consultant's final report

Output: Gender-inclusive policy and regulatory framework and support enhanced Indicator: By 2020, at least seven financial institutions' boards of directors endorsed new gender-responsive policies and practices (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.2, OP 6.2.1) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed. The Boards of directors of 10 PFIs have endorsed the reports and recommendations as of 31 May 2021. Board approval of the Gender Gap Assessment for the new 3 banks (Pan Asia, Sanasa and Union) was received by December 2022. Gender awareness workshop was conducted in Q3 2022 for 13 PFI officers with the participation of the officers of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and Ministry of Finance. SMEs' access to finance strengthened

By 2018, at least 60% of women entrepreneurs trained under the project have applied for business loans or have business plans endorsed by a business development service provider (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1, OP 1.2, OP 2.1.3, OP 2.3.1) Achievement: 84.3 Progress/Status: Completed. Out of 557 women entrepreneurs who completed the JFPR training, 398 submitted business plans which were considered as viable by banks (71.4%). Out of 470 women entrepreneurs who completed the We-Fi training, 395 submitted business plans which were considered as viable by banks (84.0%). Data Source: Consultant's final report

By 2019, at least one cluster-based loan is financed (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.2.2) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Completed. Cluster-based loan to a tea cluster was financed in 2020. Data Source: Loan documentation or confirmation from the lender

By 2020, 10% of We-Fi funded SMEs led by women report increased revenue (2015 baseline: not applicable) (OP 1.2) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the economic crisis, We-Fi project was extended until 31 December 2023. Evaluation was conducted as of December 2023 given the economic situation of the country was changed compared to project designing period. The survey was conducted on We-Fi funded WSMEs targeting projects financed during 2021-2022. Out of the 209 surveyed WSMEs, 118 (56%) demonstrated a revenue growth of 10% or more during the evaluation period. Data Source: Consultant's final report

By 2020, at least $27.1 million of financing (credit facility and We-Fi grant) provided to SMEs led by women (2015 baseline: 0) (OP 1.2.1, OP 1.3.2, OP 1.3.3, OP 2.1.3) Achievement: 11.1 Progress/Status: Completed. $ 44.1 million of blended finance provided to SMEs that are led by women as of 31 December 2023. Data Source: PMU semiannual report
